chapter: Des Moines childhood and first bands
title: Playing on Miss Nebraska's train to the Galveston beauty contest
summary: In 1926 the band was hired to play on a coach set up as a dance hall taking Miss Nebraska from Omaha to New Orleans and Galveston. In Galveston Barefield met the Alphonso Trent band.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: We played around the state there for quite a bit and played all the dances and things, after school, of course, and on weekends. In 1926 Edgar got a job playing for Miss Nebraska. Every year at that time -- I don't know if they still have it, they have an international beauty contest in Galveston, Texas. And all of the beauty queens of each state, they'd go there to compete. Well, Miss Nebraska, her entourage or whatever, hired us through Edgar Pillows to play on her train from Omaha to New Orleans and back. They set up a whole coach like a dancehall. And we played on this coach and we stopped over in different places. We stopped in a place called Hot Springs, Arkansas and Little Rock and Smack Over, Arkansas, which is an oil town. And we ended up
in New Orleans, we stayed there about a week or so. Then we went to Galveston, Texas.

And in Galveston I met Alphonso Trent (PHONETIC) who was one of the outstanding bands out there. In fact, one of the guys that was with him is here in New York now, Leo Mosley, Snub Mosley (PHONETIC). Well, he was in that band at that time. And we stayed around there about 10 days in Galveston and then we came back to Des Moines. You know, back to Omaha and back to Des Moines. But we played on this train, only on the train, for her for Miss Nebraska and her party.
